forecastReasoning.narrative:
Warm-Front Wave governs the 12Z Day 1–12Z Day 2 period. The 12Z Day 1 issuance carries a SLGT maximum, with Slight-or-greater probabilities covering 7% of the domain. The primary corridor peaks near 12Z Day 1, when mean initiation reaches 15% and expected storm coverage reaches 6%.

A baroclinic warm front focuses moisture pooling, backed low-level flow, and repeated ascent. A representative corridor sounding contains about 865 J/kg CAPE, 532 m²/s² SRH, 90 kt deep-layer shear, 1392 m LCLs, STP 2.0, and VTP 1.0. Flow increases from roughly 30 kt at 850 mb to 71 kt at 500 mb and 93 kt at 250 mb.

Maximum probabilities are 5% tornado, 5% hail, and 0% wind; tornadoes is the leading hazard signal. The analog ensemble has high agreement (94% confidence; 30 members), with mean moisture return 95%, clearing 71%, forcing 89%, and cap persistence 35%. No ensemble failure mode exceeds the reporting threshold.
supportingFactors: Coherent synoptic pattern and frontal geometry (99%)
Strong low-level hodograph curvature (532 m²/s² SRH)
Storm mode and conditional intensity support tornado potential
limitingFactors: Low or highly localized initiation signal (15% corridor mean)
Sparse expected storm coverage (6% corridor mean)
